## SECTION I SCOPE AND INTERPRETATION

## Scope

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Scope] 84.1 This Part contains rules in relation to enforcement by taking control of goods using the procedure in Schedule 12 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

## Interpretation

## 84.2 In this Part—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Tribunals Courts and Enforcement Act 2007 1 ;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (b) ‘Schedule 12’ means Schedule 12 to the Act 2 ;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (c) ‘creditor’ has the meaning given in paragraph 1(6) of Schedule 12;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (d) ‘co-owner’ has the meaning given in paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 12;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (e) ‘debtor’ has the meaning given in paragraph 1(5) of Schedule 12;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (f) ‘enforcement agent’ has the meaning given in paragraph 2(1) of Schedule 12;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (g) ‘Fees Regulations’ means the Taking Control of Goods (Fees) Regulations 2014 3 ;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (h) ‘TCG Regulations’ means the Taking Control of Goods Regulations 2013 4 ;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.2 In this Part—] (i) ‘writ of control’ and ‘warrant of control’ are to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Act.

## SECTION II WHERE AND HOW TO MAKE APPLICATIONS

## Where and how to make applications

## 84.3

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.3] (1) This rule sets out where and how applications referred to in this Part must be made.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.3] (2) Applications referred to in this Part must be made in accordance with the procedure in Part 23 as modified by this Part.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.3] (3) Where there are no pre-existing proceedings, an application referred to in this Part must be made to the County Court.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.3] (4) Where there are pre-existing proceedings, the application must be made to the High Court or the County Court in accordance with rule 23.2.

## SECTION III TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS

## 84.4

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.4] (1) This rule applies where a person seeks an order under regulation 6(3) of the TCG Regulations that a shorter notice period than the minimum period for taking control of goods set out in regulation 6(1) of those Regulations be given to the debtor.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.4] (2) The person may make an application for the order.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.4] (3) The application—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.4] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.4] (b) must be accompanied by evidence demonstrating that if the order is not made, it is likely that goods of the debtor will be moved or otherwise disposed of, in order to avoid the enforcement agent taking control of the goods.

## Application to extend the period in which to take control of goods

## 84.5

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (1) An application under regulation 9(4) of the TCG Regulations (application to extend the period in which to take control of goods) must be accompanied by—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (a) a witness statement made by the person making the application that no previous application under regulation 9(4) has been made to extend that period; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (b) the applicant’s grounds for not taking control of goods of the debtor during the period specified in regulation 9(1).

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (2) If—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (a) the application is made before the expiry of the period specified in regulation 9(1); and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (b) the court orders the period of extension,

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] the period of extension will start on the day after the expiry of the period specified in regulation 9(1), or on such later day as the court may order.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (3) If the court orders the period of extension—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (a) the applicant must serve a copy of the extension order on the debtor, and on the creditor, enforcement agent or enforcement officer as appropriate; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.5] (b) if the goods are to be taken into control by virtue of a warrant or writ of control, or of any other writ or warrant conferring the power to use the procedure in Schedule 12, the court will endorse on the warrant or writ a note of the extension.

## Application to take control of goods during prohibited hours

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to take control of goods during prohibited hours] 84.6 An application by the enforcement agent under regulation 13(2)(a) of the TCG Regulations for an order allowing goods to be taken into control during hours prohibited by regulation 13(1) of those Regulations—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to take control of goods during prohibited hours] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to take control of goods during prohibited hours] (b) must be accompanied by evidence demonstrating that if the order is not made, it is likely that goods of the debtor will be moved or otherwise disposed of, in order to avoid the enforcement agent taking control of the goods.

## Application to enter, re-enter or remain on premises otherwise than during permitted hours

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to enter, re-enter or remain on premises otherwise than during permitted hours] 84.7 An application by the enforcement agent under regulation 22(5) of the TCG Regulations for an order allowing the enforcement agent to enter, re-enter or remain on premises at times other than those permitted by regulation 22(2), (3) or (4) of those Regulations—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to enter, re-enter or remain on premises otherwise than during permitted hours] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application to enter, re-enter or remain on premises otherwise than during permitted hours] (b) must be accompanied by evidence demonstrating that if the order is not made, it is likely that goods of the debtor will be moved or otherwise disposed of, in order to avoid the enforcement agent taking control of the goods.

## 84.8

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.8] (1)  This rule applies where a person seeks an order under regulation 25(3) of the TCG Regulations that a shorter notice period than the minimum period for re-entering premises set out in regulation 25(1) of those Regulations be given to the debtor.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.8] (2) The person may make an application for the order.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.8] (3) The application—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.8] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.8] (b) must be accompanied by evidence demonstrating that if the order is not made, it is likely that goods of the debtor will be moved to be disposed of, in order to avoid the enforcement agent inspecting or removing the goods.

## 84.9

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (1)  This rule applies to an application by an enforcement agent for—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (a) the issue of a warrant under paragraph 15(1) of Schedule 12;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (b) the issue of a warrant under paragraph 20(2) of Schedule 12 allowing the use of reasonable force to enter premises; or

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (c) the inclusion in a warrant power under paragraph 21(2) of Schedule 12 to use reasonable force to enter premises.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (2) Where the application is for the issue of a warrant under paragraph 15(1) of Schedule 12, the enforcement agent must provide the court with sufficient evidence and information to satisfy the court that the conditions in paragraph 15(2) of Schedule 12 are met.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.9] (3) Where the application is for the issue of a warrant under paragraph 20(2) or 21(2) of Schedule 12, the enforcement agent must provide the court with sufficient evidence and information to satisfy the court that the conditions set out in regulation 28(2) of the TCG Regulations have been met.

## 84.10

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.10] (1)  This rule applies to an application by an enforcement agent for the issue of a warrant under paragraph 31(1) of Schedule 12 allowing the use of reasonable force in relation to goods on the highway.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.10] (2) The enforcement agent must provide the court with sufficient evidence and information to satisfy the court that the conditions set out in regulation 29(2) of the TCG Regulations have been met.

## Application for sale otherwise than by public auction

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application for sale otherwise than by public auction] 84.11 (1)  This rule applies to an application by an enforcement agent for an order for sale otherwise than by public auction under paragraph 41(2) of Schedule 12 (‘alternative sale application’).

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application for sale otherwise than by public auction] (2) Where the enforcement agent has made a statement to the court under paragraph 41(4) of Schedule 12 (reason to believe that an enforcement power has become exercisable by another creditor against the debtor or co-owner), the alternative sale application must be accompanied by—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application for sale otherwise than by public auction] (a) a list of the name and address of every other creditor that the enforcement agent has reason to believe has an exercisable enforcement power against the debtor or co-owner and a explanation of why the enforcement agent has such a belief; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application for sale otherwise than by public auction] (b) a copy of the notice of application required by paragraph 41(5) of Schedule 12 and proof that the notice has been served on such other creditors not less than 4 days before the day fixed for the hearing of the application.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > Application for sale otherwise than by public auction] (3) Every person to whom notice of the application was given may attend and be heard on the hearing of the application.

## Application in relation to disposal of abandoned goods

## 84.12

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.12] (1)  This rule applies to an application by the enforcement agent under regulation 47(5) of the TCG Regulations for an order for the disposal of goods abandoned by the debtor.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.12] (2) If the enforcement agent applies for an order for disposal by way of donation to a charitable organisation or destruction of goods, the enforcement agent must explain in the application why the enforcement agent does not wish the goods to be made available for a further period of collection.

## Application by the debtor for a remedy in relation to goods taken into control

## 84.13

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (1)  This rule applies where the debtor wishes to bring proceedings under paragraph 66 of Schedule 12 5 for—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (a) breach of a provision of Schedule 12; or

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (b) enforcement action taken under a defective instrument.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (2) The debtor may bring proceedings by way of an application.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (3) The application must be accompanied by evidence of how—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (a) the provisions of Schedule 12 are alleged to have been breached; or

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.13] (b) the instrument is alleged to be defective.

## Application by the enforcement agent for exceptional disbursements

## 84.14

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (1)  This rule applies to an application by an enforcement agent for exceptional disbursements under regulation 10 of the Fees Regulations.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (2) The application must be accompanied by—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (a) evidence of the creditor’s consent to the application; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (b) evidence that the disbursements to which the application relate are necessary for effective enforcement of the sum to be recovered, having regard to all the circumstances including—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (i) the amount of the sum to be recovered; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (ii) the nature and value of the goods which have been taken into control, or which it is sought to take into control.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.14] (3) Where the application is made before the goods are taken into control, it may be made without notice.

## Application where there is a dispute regarding a co-owner’s share of proceeds

## 84.15

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (1) This rule applies to an application under regulation 15 of the Fees Regulations to determine the amount of the proceeds payable to a co-owner.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (2) The applicant must file with the application—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (a) evidence of the enforcement power;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (b) a copy of the itemised list of goods sold or otherwise disposed of required by regulation 14(1)(a) of the Fees Regulations;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (c) a copy of the statement of the sum received in relation to each item required by regulation 14(1)(b)(i) of the Fees Regulations;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (d) a copy of the statement of the proceeds required by regulation 14(1)(b)(ii) of the Fees Regulations;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (e) a copy of the statement of the application of the proceeds required by regulation 14(1)(b)(iii) of the Fees Regulations;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (f) evidence that the share of proceeds paid to the co-owner was not proportionate to the co-owner’s interest in the goods sold.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] (3) The applicant must serve a copy of the application notice in accordance with table 1.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Table 1

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Applicant | Those to be served with a copy of the application notice

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Co-owner | Any other co-owners; creditor; debtor; enforcement agent

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Creditor | Co-owners; debtor; enforcement agent

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Debtor | Co-owners; creditor; enforcement agent

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.15] Enforcement agent | Co-owners; creditor; debtor

## Disputes about the amount of fees or disbursements recoverable under the Fees Regulations

## 84.16

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (1)  This rule applies where—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (a)there is a dispute about the amount of fees or disbursements, other than exceptional disbursements, recoverable under the Fees Regulations; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (b)a party wishes the court to assess the amounts recoverable under regulation 16 of the Fees Regulations.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (2) A party may make an application to the court to assess the amounts.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (3) The application must be accompanied by—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (a) evidence of the amount of fees or disbursements in dispute;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (b) evidence that the fees or disbursements in dispute were not applicable, as the debt had been settled before the stage where it would have been necessary to incur those fees or expenses;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (c) evidence that, because the enforcement agent was instructed to use the TCG procedure in relation to the same debtor but in respect of more than one enforcement power where the enforcement powers could reasonably be exercised at the same time, regulation 11 of the Fees Regulations should have been applied;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (d) evidence that the fee due and any disbursements for the enforcement stage, first enforcement stage, or first and second enforcement stage, as appropriate, are not recoverable under regulation 12 of the Fees Regulations; or

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.16] (e) where the dispute concerns the amount of the percentage fee, calculated in accordance with regulation 7 of the Fees Regulations, evidence of the amount of the sum to be recovered.

## SECTION IV PROCEEDINGS IN RELATION TO CERTIFICATES UNDER SECTION 64 OF THE 2007 ACT

## Interpretation

## 84.17 In this Section—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.17 In this Section—] (a) ‘Certification Regulations’ means the Certification of Enforcement Agents Regulations 2014 6 ;

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.17 In this Section—] (b) ‘applicant’, ‘certificate’, ‘certificated person’ and ‘complainant’ have the meanings given in regulation 2 of the Certification Regulations.

## Application for issue of a certificate under section 64 of the 2007 Act

## 84.18

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (1) This rule applies to an application for the issue of a certificate under section 64 of the 2007 Act.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (2) The application must be made to the Civil National Business Centre, using the approved form.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (3) The application must specify one of the County Court hearing centres listed in Practice Direction 84 as the centre at which the application is to be heard.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (4) The application must, in addition to the matters specified in rule 23.6, provide evidence that the applicant fulfils the requirements of regulation 3(b) of the Certification Regulations, and in particular—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (a) the application must be accompanied by the documents specified in Practice Direction 84; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (b) the additional documents specified in Practice Direction 84 must be produced to the court on the day of the hearing.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (5) If any reasons have been submitted to the court in response to the notice of the application required by regulation 4(5) of the Certification Regulations, a copy of those reasons must be sent to the applicant at least 7 days before the hearing, and the applicant may respond both in writing and at the hearing.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (6) The applicant must also file such further evidence as the court may direct.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (7) The applicant must attend for examination on the day of the hearing.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.18] (8) Rules 23.2, 23.4, 23.7, 23.8, 23.9 and 23.10 do not apply to an application to which this rule applies.

## Issue of replacement certificates and surrender of certificates

## 84.19

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.19] (1) Where changes are required to be notified and the certificate produced under regulation 8 of the Certification Regulations, the changes must be notified to, and the certificate produced at, the County Court hearing centre at which the certificate was issued.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.19] (2) Where a certificate is required to be surrendered under regulation 12 of the Certification Regulations, the certificate must be surrendered to the County Court hearing centre at which the certificate was issued.

## Complaints as to fitness to hold a certificate

## 84.20

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (1) This rule applies to a complaint under regulation 9(1) of the Certification Regulations.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (2) The complaint must be submitted to the County Court hearing centre at which the certificate was issued, using the approved form.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (3) A copy of the complaint must be sent to the applicant at least 14 days before the hearing, and the applicant may respond both in writing and at the hearing.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (4) The complainant is not liable for any costs incurred by the certificated person in responding to the complaint, unless paragraph (5) applies.

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (5) The court may order the complainant to pay such costs as it considers reasonable if it is satisfied that the complaint—

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (a) discloses no reasonable grounds for considering that the certificated person is not a fit person to hold a certificate; and

[PART 84 – ENFORCEMENT BY TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS > 84.20] (b) amounts to an abuse of the court’s process.
